f1.quote: Increasing Fe and Co, reducing Mn, and lowering P from 20 to 15 at.%

f2.quote: examined both as a slower-cooled arc-melted ingot and as ~20 μm melt-spun ribbon

f3.quote: Arc melting was performed under 99.999% Ar in a water-cooled copper crucible.

f4.quote: DSC heating/cooling used Ar and 20 K/min.

f5.quote: Increasing Fe and Co, reducing Mn, and lowering P from 20 to 15 at.% decreases primary solid-solution crystallization and limits high-temperature phosphide formation, shifting solidification toward cooperative eutectic growth.

f6.quote: A eutectic-dominated solidification structure comprising fine, predominantly rod-like eutectic colonies; under slower cooling, inter-colony partitioning produces an Fe–Ni–Mn-rich solid solution and P/Cr-rich phosphides

f7.quote: Rapid cooling suppresses elemental segregation and phosphide nucleation, preserving amorphous order

f8.quote: Relative to the prior Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy, the modified alloy should exhibit a simpler, predominantly eutectic transformation sequence

f9.quote: rapid melt spinning should yield a fully amorphous state

f10.quote: On reheating, the amorphous ribbon devitrifies through sequential TM-rich ordering, possible early phosphide formation, and final formation of a TM solid solution plus P-rich phosphides.
